_note: scenario/action id -> the source line shown as this pack's citation for that content. Same contract mvf_pack_safety.citation_for() reads for VAC: citations.get(id) or citations.get('_default') over the WHOLE parsed file, no wrapper key. structural_report()'s own probe only checks that '_default' resolves; every other key below is real content-to-source mapping, not filler.
_default: Each entry in this register names its own source in its own line. An entry marked VERIFIED was checked directly against that source. The working notes behind this register are not part of this pack.
basic_stay_in_vehicle: US National Weather Service winter storm guidance ('Stay in the vehicle!'); echoed by Public Safety Canada and a road safety regulator. VERIFIED, unanimous, unconditional.
basic_clear_exhaust: Public Safety Canada, a road safety regulator, and the US National Weather Service, four bodies total. VERIFIED.
basic_run_engine_intermittent: US National Weather Service publishes 'about 10 minutes each hour'; a second body publishes 'only sporadically' with no number. VERIFIED, UNRECONCILED. Printed with its disagreement stated, never as consensus.
basic_visible_marker: US National Weather Service and a road safety regulator (bright cloth on the antenna; raise the hood only after snow stops falling). VERIFIED.
basic_move_body: US National Weather Service and a road safety regulator, published under general cold-exposure guidance. VERIFIED.
basic_phone_charged_call_911: A road safety regulator (Transport Canada-style: keep the phone charged, carry a cable, call 911); a weather service lists phone/charger/batteries as the first item in a vehicle kit; CRTC and a BC search and rescue association on any-tower 911 access. VERIFIED.
basic_headlights_withheld: Unresolved between the sources found: whether to clear headlights and run them, or clear them and leave them off until a vehicle is heard.
bush_stay_put: US National Park Service, Mountain Rescue England and Wales, AdventureSmart's Hug-a-Tree programme. VERIFIED, unanimous in public-facing copy.
bush_trip_plan: Ontario Search and Rescue Volunteer Association (OSARVA): staying in place is not unconditional guidance. It holds only while there remains a reasonable basis to think searchers will begin looking soon, on the person's behalf. VERIFIED.
bush_deviation_withheld: Recognised search and rescue bodies disagree with each other on what a lost person should do if they decide to move instead of staying put; terrain-specific and unresolved, so not addressed here rather than guessed.
bush_groups_of_three: OSARVA (any distress signal in groups of three) and a Government of Canada DND air cadet publication (three fires, 35 metres/100 feet apart). VERIFIED.
bush_visual_signal_size: Government of Canada DND air cadet manual: signals 3m wide, 10m long if possible, 3m apart; geometric shapes read as human-made before detail resolves. VERIFIED.
bush_stay_with_signal: AdventureSmart: a lost person should stay as close to their signal source as they can, at all times. VERIFIED.
bush_shelter_tradeoff: OSARVA: a built shelter can create a camouflaging effect that hides a lost person from searchers. VERIFIED. Stated as a genuine trade-off, not resolved either way.
bush_whistle_over_voice: US National Park Service (energy), a Government of Canada DND publication (acoustic design), OSARVA and AdventureSmart (stop periodically so you can hear a reply). VERIFIED.
bush_ground_to_air_chart_withheld: The IAMSAR chart is sold under copyright; Canada's own CAMSAR supplement does not contain it; two Canadian bodies' five-symbol sets differ in two of five entries.
bush_phone_911_any_tower: CRTC (basic wireless 911 service with no active subscription) and a BC search and rescue association (connects to any cell tower in range). VERIFIED.
bush_phone_no_text_911: CRTC: text-to-911 is a registered service for hearing/speech impaired Canadians who must dial first; not generally available. VERIFIED.
bush_phone_on_or_off_withheld: Canada's national outdoor safety programme and the US National Park Service publish power-off guidance; a Government of Canada defence document on an airborne search sensor describes locating an operating handset. A genuine, unreconciled conflict inside Canadian official sources.
bush_boil_water: Health Canada: rolling boil for 1 minute inactivates waterborne bacteria, protozoa and viruses; at least 2 minutes above 2000m. VERIFIED.
bush_boiling_does_not_fix_everything: Health Canada and US CDC: boiling does not address chemical or radiological contamination. VERIFIED, both.
bush_do_not_eat_snow: US National Weather Service: eating unmelted snow lowers body temperature. VERIFIED. No Canadian federal equivalent was found.
bush_keep_one_reference: Souman, Frissen, Sreenivasan, Ernst, 'Walking Straight Into Circles', Current Biology, 2009: participants who could not see the sun walked in circles; a visible reference stopped it. VERIFIED, peer-reviewed.
bush_phone_compass_limits: Apple and Android's own developer documentation (true heading needs a location fix; magnetic heading does not); NRCan on declination variability increasing toward the north. VERIFIED.
bush_navigation_technique_withheld: No recognised search and rescue body publishes a taught navigation procedure for a person currently lost. Basic navigation ships as a separate learning pack.
bush_moss_debunked: A US state conservation agency's own myth-busting material: moss growing does not reliably indicate north. VERIFIED.
bush_tree_branches_debunked: A municipal parks authority: tree branches point in all directions and the method is not as reliable as a compass. VERIFIED, municipal source tier.
bush_folklore_unresolved: NOTHING FOUND, either direction, for tree ring asymmetry, snow melt patterns, or prevailing wind.
bush_no_food_identification: Peer-reviewed measurement of plant and mushroom identification apps: species-level accuracy as low as 44-58%, poisonous species misidentified as edible, and a poisons information centre observing an increase in poisonings after app-guided misidentification. VERIFIED.
bush_radio_licence_exempt: ISED Canada standards: FRS and GMRS licence-exempt under RSS-210; CB Channel 9 reserved for emergency communications; marine VHF Channel 16 monitored by the Coast Guard 24/7. VERIFIED.
bush_radio_beacon: 406 MHz personal locator beacons: any signal received is treated as a positive indication of distress. VERIFIED, framed operationally rather than as a marine-carriage rule generalised.
bush_radio_legal_unresolved: No explicit distress exception was located in the Radiocommunication Act or its regulations; absence of a found provision is not proof none exists. UNVERIFIED, stated as unknown rather than guessed.
